## Intent Fix vLLM issue #32268 (vllm-project/vllm on GitHub): refactor Int8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig boolean fields to QuantKey, following the existing FP8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig pattern. Mechanical, compiler-checkable change, validated by the repo's own tests. ## What Changed - `Int8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig` drops the `is_channelwise` and `is_static_input_scheme` booleans (and the related TODO). It now carries `weight_quant_key` and `activation_quant_key` `QuantKey` fields, like `FP8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig`. `input_symmetric` stays as a field. `init_int8_linear_kernel` takes the two keys and sets `input_symmetric` from `activation_quant_key.symmetric`. - The int8 scaled-mm kernels (`aiter`, `cpu`, `cutlass`, `triton`, `zentorch`) read the QuantKeys instead of the removed booleans. The compressed-tensors W8A8 int8 scheme builds the keys through a new `_int8_quant_keys` helper that maps strategy, static/dynamic input and symmetry to the `kInt8*` keys. The Quark W8A8 int8 scheme is updated for the new `init_int8_linear_kernel` signature. - `test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` and `test_quant_activation_contract.py` are updated to build configs with QuantKeys. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This is a mechanical refactor of one config's fields to QuantKey. Every consumer and caller I checked maps the old booleans to the same behavior, and no old-field references remain. ## Testing On macOS I could not run the repo's own tests: the selection test segfaulted on its first case (no compiled vllm._C), and the CUDA/CPU kernels and model loading cannot run here. I instead drove the changed code directly in a disposable venv. The new config accepted QuantKeys, Zentorch can_implement returned the right accept/reject for channel, tensor, static-activation and asymmetric configs, and the compressed-tensors QuantKey mapping gave the right static/dynamic, symmetric and group-shape keys for all 8 combinations. Not driven: the Cutlass, Triton, CPU and Aiter kernel paths, the Quark scheme, and the two changed test files. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 2 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Zentorch can_implement accepts per-channel dynamic symmetric config and rejects per-tensor, static-activation and asymmetric configs when built from QuantKeys | ✅ pass | live | Ad-hoc script output: (True, None); 'requires per-channel weight quantization.'; 'requires dynamic activation quantization.'; 'requires symmetric activation quantization.' | | Compressed-tensors scheme maps channel/tensor strategy and static/dynamic, sym/asym to the correct QuantKeys (all 8 combinations) | ✅ pass | live | Ad-hoc script printing _int8_quant_keys for every combination; the keys have the expected static flag, group shape and symmetry | | Repo tests (test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection, test_quant_activation_contract) and Cutlass/Triton/CPU/Aiter kernel paths pass end-to-end | ⏸️ untested | no | The host is macOS with no compiled vllm._C, CUDA or ROCm, so these tests and kernel paths cannot run. To validate, run them in CI or on a Linux CPU/GPU machine with a built vLLM. | - Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (2m14s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/ScaledMMLinearKernel.py:28` - `input_symmetric` is kept as a separate field in Int8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig, but `init_int8_linear_kernel` always derives it from `activation_quant_key.symmetric`. Tests build configs that set it independently, so the two can disagree. The intent says to convert the boolean fields to QuantKey following the FP8 pattern; this leftover is a minor redundancy and does not cause a bug on any current path.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 warning - ⚠️ live validation verdict: inconclusive (2 of 3 scenarios were driven live against the product); untested: Repo tests (test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection, test_quant_activation_contract) and Cutlass/Triton/CPU/Aiter kernel paths pass end-to-end - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 2 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Zentorch can_implement accepts per-channel dynamic symmetric config and rejects per-tensor, static-activation and asymmetric configs when built from QuantKeys | ✅ pass | live | Ad-hoc script output: (True, None); 'requires per-channel weight quantization.'; 'requires dynamic activation quantization.'; 'requires symmetric activation quantization.' | | Compressed-tensors scheme maps channel/tensor strategy and static/dynamic, sym/asym to the correct QuantKeys (all 8 combinations) | ✅ pass | live | Ad-hoc script printing _int8_quant_keys for every combination; the keys have the expected static flag, group shape and symmetry | | Repo tests (test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection, test_quant_activation_contract) and Cutlass/Triton/CPU/Aiter kernel paths pass end-to-end | ⏸️ untested | no | The host is macOS with no compiled vllm._C, CUDA or ROCm, so these tests and kernel paths cannot run. To validate, run them in CI or on a Linux CPU/GPU machine with a built vLLM. | - `Built a disposable venv with torch and vLLM common requirements (removed afterwards)` - `Ad-hoc script building Int8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig from QuantKeys and calling ZentorchInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.can_implement for 4 cases` - `Ad-hoc script calling _int8_quant_keys for all 8 combinations of strategy, static/dynamic and symmetric/asymmetric` - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py` (segfaulted on macOS)
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.
